newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela public sector strike goes into tenth day.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela public sector strike goes into tenth day.

text.p: Protesting Venezuelan public sector workers extended their strike for the tenth day Monday as they waited for 100 billion bolivars ($212 million) of salary bonuses to be paid, trade union officials said.

Government spending requests for the bonuses, first promised in February, were approved last week, but must be processed by the Finance Ministry and then the National Treasury before they can be paid.
"Nobody's in there," said Israel Coronil, Secretary General of the National Federation of Public Workers, as he stood outside the Finance Ministry.
"The only thing they're processing is their end-of-the-year party," he said, watching waiters setting out chairs, drinks and canapes.
The strike, billed as a 48-hour stoppage when it began, is the most serious labor conflict since President Rafael Caldera took office in February 1994.
The Labor Ministry has played down the strike, saying less than 10 percent of the Union's 1.3 million members have stopped work -- a claim rejected by union heads.

Some 27,000 doctors and medical staff joined the strike last week asking for a salary raise to World Health Organization recommended levels of $1,000 per month. Venezuelan doctors currently earn an average $127 per month.
